The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Sri.Lakshmipathi, in the road traffic accident that took place on 27.02.2024.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 27.02.2024 at 10.20 a.m. the deceased was proceeding as a pedestrian on DVG road, Bagepalli town, when he reached near Mutton Market in order to cross the road, at that time, driver of the Water Tanker Tractor bearing Reg. No.KA-40-B-0534 Sidrah Sulaiman vs Sandesh K.C on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147730650/
2 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased and caused the accident, due to which said Lakshmipathi sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately injured was shifted to Govt., Hospital, Bagepalli for first aid, then shifted to Govt., Hospital, Chikkaballapura, later he was shifted to Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and died in the said hospital during the course of treatment.

After conducting the post mortem, dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards medical and funeral expenses.
3. It is stated that prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 70 years and doing Tailoring work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Water Tanker Tractor bearing Reg.No. KA- 40-B-0534.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
4. Inspite service of summons, the 1st respondent remained absent, hence he was placed exparte.
Upon service of summons, 2nd respondent appeared before the court through its counsel and filed written statement.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It has denied the age,
income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the medical and funeral expenses of the deceased.

Further contended that, Water Tanker Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-40/B-0534 belongs to 1st respondent and took specific contention that the first respondent does not hold any Insurance with this department, hence KGID/respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Further contended that, the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of deceased himself, as there was no Zebra crossing at the accident spot.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, this court has framed following issues:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 27.02.2024 at 10.20 a.m. when the deceased was crossing the road near Mutton Market, DVG Road, Bagepalli Town, at that time,
the driver of the water tanker bearing Reg. No.KA-40-B- Sidrah Sulaiman vs Sandesh K.C on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147730650/
3 0534 by driving the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased, caused the accident, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Lakshmipathi?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case, 1 st petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to 14 documents.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 did not adduce its side evidence.
8. Heard the arguments.

9. My findings on the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 ...

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 ...

Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4 ...
As per final order

For the following:
 REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 27-02-2024 at 10.20 a.m. when the deceased was proceeding as a pedestrian on DVG road, Bagepalli town, when he reached near Mutton Market in order to cross the road, at that time, driver of the Water Tanker Tractor bearing Reg. No.KA-40/B-0534 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased and caused the accident, due to which said Lakshmipathi sustained grievous injuries and died in the hospital on 4-3-2024 during the course of treatment.

It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the driver of Water Tanker Tractor and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
11.

In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R,
F.I.S, Spot mahazar, Inquest report, P.M. report, further Statement/complaint, Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, reply to the said notice and Charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.

On the other hand,
respondent No.2 not adduced any oral or documentary evidence on its behalf.
12. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.

There are four basic elements that a person Sidrah Sulaiman vs Sandesh K.C on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147730650/
4 has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

entities.text: person Sidrah Sulaiman vs Sandesh K.C
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

13. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened near Mutton Market, on DVG road, Bagapalli Town, the driver of Water Tanker Tractor came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased and caused the accident.
Though the Respondent No.2 filed its written statement by denying the petition averments, but not adduced any evidence on its behalf to disprove the contention of the petitioners.
Therefore the evidence of the petitioners is unchallenged and un- rebutted, there is no evidence to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.
14. It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P3 being the Spot Mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3, it reflects that deceased was crossing the road, the driver of water tanker with out observe who have cross the road,
came in a negligent manner in high speed and dashed against the deceased person, due to the said act deceased person fell down on the road and got injured.
If the driver of water tanker drove it in a normal speed, by observing the pedestrians who cross the road then he would certainly avoid the accident.
Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P9 was also filed as against the driver of the water tanker.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3 coupled with Ex.P9 charge sheet it is Sidrah Sulaiman vs Sandesh K.C on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147730650/
5 crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the water tanker driver.
15.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the owner of the water tanker who is the Respondent No.1 is not appeared even after service of notice to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the driver of Lorry and he was charge sheeted.
16. Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.

The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the offending vehicle water tanker tractor bearing Reg.
No. KA.40/B-0534 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2 and 3:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the death of Sri.Lakshmipathi occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioners claimed that, Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards of deceased and petitioners No.1 and 2
, and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
As per the cause title of the petition, age of the petitioner No.1 is shown as 60 years and petitioner No.2 is shown as 17 years.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners No.1 & 2 are the legal representatives and dependents on the income of the deceased Sri.Lakshmipathi, hence they are entitled for compensation.

Sidrah Sulaiman vs Sandesh K.C on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147730650/
6 18.
The petitioners have contended that the deceased was doing Tailor work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In order to prove the same, petitioners have not produced any documents before the court.
Therefore, considering the occupation of the deceased and year of the accident, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,500/- per month.
19. It is stated that the deceased was aged 70 years at the time of the accident.
The petitioners have produced Adhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P9 which shows the date of birth of the deceased as 01.01.1945.
The accident occurred on 27.02.2024.

Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident is considered as 79 years and the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '5'.
20.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 79 years.
Therefore, the petitioners are not entitled to claim future prospects.
The deceased died leaving behind 2 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.11,000/- p.m. (Rs.16,500/- - Rs.5,500/- = Rs.11,000/-).
21.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,667/- p.m. and the multiplier '05' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.6,60,000/- (Rs.11,000 X 12 X 5).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.6,60,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
22. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioners have produced Medical bill worth Rs.5,100/- as per Ex.P14, which they have incurred towards medication of the deceased at the time of hospitalization due to accidental injuries.
I have examined the same.

Since the deceased was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment at the time of accident, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioners towards medication of the deceased to the tune of Rs.5,100/-.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,100/- under this head.

23. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.
Sidrah Sulaiman vs Sandesh K.C on 4 December, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147730650/
7

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
24.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners No.2 is entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of father causes great shock and agony to the daughter of the deceased and she lost the love and affection towards her father.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.48,400/- under the head of Filial consortium.

25. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation under the heads Amount  1 Towards loss of dependency Rs. 6,60,000-00  2 Towards Medical expenses Rs. 5,100-00  3 Towards loss of Consortium to the Rs. 48,400-00  petitioner No.1  4 Towards loss to estate Rs. 18,150-00  5 Towards transportation of dead body Rs. 18,150-00  funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses  6 Towards loss of Filial consortium to Rs. 48,400-00  petitioner No.2 (Rs.48,400 x 1)
 Total Rs. 7,98,200-00

In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,98,200/-.
26.
With regard to the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the 1st petitioner is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter of the deceased.

Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No.1 & 2 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 70:30.
27.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
28. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Water Tanker Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-40/B-0534.
After issuance of notice respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he was placed exparte.

The respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel Sidrah Sulaiman vs Sandesh K.C on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147730650/
8 and filed objection statement.

Respondent No.2 has seriously disputed its liability by contending the water tanker tractor bearing NO.KA-40/B-0534 belongs to first respondent does not hold any insurance with this department, hence respondent No.2/KGID is not liable to pay any compensation.
In support of its contention, the respondent No.2 did not adduce any oral or documentary evidence on its behalf.

Hence, from the evidence available on record it can be held that the respondent No.2 has not issued policy in respect of offending vehicle and was not in force as on the date of accident, for which respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1/ R.C.
owner.
On perusal of Ex.P9 Charge sheet also, police have invoked section 196 of MV Act, for driving a motor vehicle without third-party insurance, in violation of Section 146.
Hence, respondent No.1 being the R.C owner is liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation.
Accordingly, I have answered issue No.2 in the Affirmative and issued No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.7,98,200/- (Rupees Seven lakhs ninety eight thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
Petition in respect of Respondent No.2 is dismissed.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows:
 Petitioner No.1 - 70%
 Petitioner No.2 - 30%
Further it is ordered that, 30% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioner No.1 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 2 years in her name and remaining 60% of the amount is ordered to be released in her favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.

The entire share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioner No.2 is ordered to be deposited in her name in any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner for a period of 3 years,
with a liberty to the petitioner No.1 to draw periodical interest.

9

Draw award accordingly.
